best_for: Windows users who need to sign and encrypt files and Outlook mail with OpenPGP or S/MIME, whether a journalist, a lawyer or an IT admin rolling it out to staff.
description:
Gpg4win is the official GnuPG distribution for Windows, kept up by the developers of GnuPG. Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) backed its creation, and GnuPG follows the BSI's advice on algorithms and key lengths.

You can sign and encrypt whole folders, or many files at once, into a single file the recipient can check and open. You can also make and verify SHA-256, SHA-1 or MD5 checksums to prove a file has not changed. In Outlook, attachments are encrypted together with the message body, and Kleopatra picks the right certificate from the email address. Smart cards work with both OpenPGP and S/MIME. You can fetch certificates from key servers and certify the public key of someone you trust.

points.title: Four pieces in one installer
points.text: You get GnuPG for the actual encryption, Kleopatra to manage OpenPGP and S/MIME certificates, GpgOL for Outlook, and GpgEX for right-click encryption in Explorer. The old GPA key manager was dropped in 4.1.0.

points.title: Classic Outlook is the target
points.text: GpgOL supports classic Outlook 2021, 2024 and Office 365, 32-bit and 64-bit, over Exchange or IMAP and SMTP. Outlook 2010 and later may still work but are unsupported. A web add-in for the new Outlook ships from 5.0.0 and is marked experimental.

points.title: 64-bit Windows 10 and 11 only
points.text: Since 5.0.0 Gpg4win supports only 64-bit systems, on Windows 10 version 1809 or later and Windows 11. On older Windows the project points to the plain command-line GnuPG installer instead.

points.title: Free software, no account
points.text: Gpg4win is free software under the GPL with no sign-up. The project asks for donations to fund its work.

points.title: Keep it current
points.text: Version 5.1.2 arrived on November 20, 2026 as a security update. For encryption software, falling behind on updates is the bigger risk than a new bug.

points.title: Install details
points.text: The installer is 64-bit and installs for all users, so it needs administrator rights. The Windows listing keeps 19 versions, which helps when an Outlook add-in update clashes with your setup.
